newsitem.title: CUBA: Rescuers look for Cuban plane's flight recorder.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers look for Cuban plane's flight recorder.

text.p: Cuban rescue workers searched the sea off the eastern city of Santiago de Cuba on Monday for the flight recorder from a Cuban passenger plane that crashed three days ago, killing all 44 people on board.

The Cuban civil aviation institute said in a statement that retrieving the flight recorder would be crucial to finding out how the accident occured. It did not give details of how the search was being carried out, but it was being led by the coast guard and the armed forces.
The Cubana de Aviacion An-24 plane, a Soviet-built Antonov, plunged into the sea late on Friday, just a few minutes after taking off from Santiago on a scheduled domestic flight to Havana.
Six Spaniards and two Brazilians were among the 39 passengers. There were five crew members aboard.
Cuban authorities have so far given no indication of what might have caused the twin-engined turbo-prop plane to crash.
Monday's statement by the civil aviation institute said the bodies of 20 people had been recovered, 11 of which had been identified.

Cuban state television showed showed rescue workers at the Santiago port sifting through a small pile of personal items recovered from the sea, including family photographs, clothing and sandals. It also showed them bringing ashore a badly mutilated and swollen body.
The communist-ruled island's worst airline disaster was in September 1989, when 126 people were killed when a Cuban airlines plane crashed near Havana.
